01.event: Levi went out and taught a ruling about writing a divorce document on forbidden items, first in Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi's name and then as an unattributed majority view.
01.turn: The audience withheld praise when he named Rabbi, but praised him when he gave the same ruling in the name of the majority.
01.outcome: From this reaction it was concluded that the law follows Rabbi's view.
01.summary: Levi went out and taught a ruling that Rabbi (Yehuda HaNasi) had stated, naming Rabbi as the source. The listeners did not praise him. When he taught the same ruling in the name of the majority, they praised him. This showed that the law follows Rabbi's view.

02.event: Aher saw the tongue of Hutzpit the interpreter, executed by the government, being dragged along the street by a pig.
02.turn: He asked whether a mouth that produced pearls should lap dust.
02.summary: One account of why Aher lost his faith says he saw the tongue of Hutzpit the interpreter, who had been executed, dragged along by a pig. He asked how a mouth that had produced pearls could end up lapping dust. With that, he went out and sinned.

03.actor: The neighbors of a gentile superintendent, and the rabbis they consulted
03.event: Neighbors asked a gentile superintendent to rent them his domain so they could carry on Shabbat, he refused, and they went to rabbis to ask whether they could rent it from his wife.
03.turn: Rav Yehuda bar Oshaya and Rav Mattana had no answer ready, and only Rav Yehuda ruled.
03.outcome: Rav Yehuda told them, in Shmuel's name, that a man's wife may establish an eiruv without his knowledge.
03.summary: A gentile superintendent living near Rav Yehuda bar Oshaya refused to rent his domain to his neighbors. They asked Rav Yehuda bar Oshaya whether they could rent it from his wife, and he had no answer. Rav Mattana also had none. They then came to Rav Yehuda, who told them that Shmuel had ruled that a man's wife may establish an eiruv without his knowledge.

04.missing: Legal discussion with a cited baraita about a testimony; no narrative.

05.event: The Sages asked Rabbi Elai where Rabbi Abbahu was, and he answered with a cryptic wordplay.
05.turn: His answer was a riddle, hinting that Abbahu had gone to consult the Nasi and the Sages of the south.
05.summary: The Sages asked Rabbi Elai to show them where Rabbi Abbahu was hiding, just as they had earlier asked Abbahu about Elai. Elai replied in a riddle of wordplay, saying Abbahu had consulted the one who crowns (the Nasi) and gone south to Mephibosheth. The Gemara explains that this means he went to the Sages of the south.
05.missing: No resolution of whether they found Abbahu; it is a verbal exchange rather than a developed story.

06.missing: A halakhic proof from Shmuel's passing through the city gates, with no event.

07.actor: Rav Nahman, Ulla, Avimei and Rav Hiyya bar Ami
07.event: A man whose betrothed wife had died came before the sitting scholars, and they told him to bury her or pay her marriage contract.
07.turn: Rav Hiyya objected by citing the teaching that a man does not inherit his betrothed and that she collects her contract only if he dies.
07.outcome: Rav Hiyya inferred that a betrothed woman who dies has no marriage contract; the passage does not say what the man did.
07.summary: A man whose betrothed wife had died came before several scholars. They told him to either bury her or pay her marriage contract. Rav Hiyya protested that a teaching says the husband does not inherit his betrothed, and from it inferred that a betrothed woman who dies has no marriage contract.
07.missing: What happened to the man; the ending is a legal inference.

08.missing: A legal answer in a dispute; the 'incident' in Tzippori is only mentioned in passing.

09.event: Rava was silent when Rav Hamnuna raised an objection to him, and after Hamnuna left he worked out possible answers.
09.turn: He considered answering with Rabbi Elazar's opinion, doubted it, then found a baraita showing Rabbi Elazar rules this way even in this case.
09.outcome: He concluded the objection could be dismissed because the baraita follows Rabbi Elazar.
09.summary: Rav Hamnuna objected to Rava from a baraita, and Rava had no answer and stayed silent. After Hamnuna left, Rava chided himself for not saying it follows Rabbi Elazar. He doubted that, then found a baraita showing Rabbi Elazar rules the same way here, resolving the difficulty.
09.missing: It is mostly internal legal reasoning rather than external events.

10.missing: A scriptural question about how virginity was determined, answered with a method; no event is narrated.

11.actor: The residents of a crooked alleyway in Sura, and Rav Hisda
11.event: The residents rolled up a mat and placed it at the turn of the alleyway as a side post, and Rav Hisda ruled on it.
11.turn: Rav Hisda said it fit neither Rav's nor Shmuel's opinion because the wind would blow the mat away.
11.outcome: The mat was ruled ineffective, unless a peg were fixed in it.
11.summary: In Sura, the residents of a crooked alleyway rolled up a mat and placed it at the bend to serve as a side post. Rav Hisda said this satisfied neither Rav nor Shmuel, since the wind would blow it over. The mat counts for nothing, unless it is attached with a peg.
11.missing: It is a ruling on a case, not a story with a developed arc.

12.missing: A description of Rabbi Abbahu's habitual practice in different places, used as a legal proof.

13.actor: Rav Pappa and Yehuda bar Mareimar
13.event: Rav Pappa went to write his son's marriage contract and pressed Yehuda bar Mareimar to enter the bride's father's house with him, though Yehuda did not want to because his presence would pressure the father to give a larger dowry.
13.turn: Yehuda entered and sat silent, so the father kept increasing the dowry until he had given everything he had.
13.outcome: Yehuda said he did not want even that much, the father offered to retract, and Yehuda told him to keep his word although it was not to his liking.
13.summary: Rav Pappa went to have his son's marriage contract written, and Yehuda bar Mareimar came out to greet him but balked at entering the bride's father's house. After Rav Pappa pressed him, Yehuda entered and sat silent. The father, thinking he was angry, kept writing more and more of his property into the dowry. When Yehuda explained that he disliked even that, the father offered to retract. Yehuda said he had not meant him to retract, only that the arrangement was not to his liking.

14.event: The Sages reversed the two attributions in a dispute over a child's gift and sent word to Rav Mordekhai, who corrected them.
14.turn: Rav Mordekhai recalled the actual incident, when Rav Ashi stood with one foot on the step and answered the question about a child's gift.
14.outcome: He had them tell Mar bar Rav Ashi that his father had ruled the gift valid in all cases.
14.summary: Abaye asked about a child's gift, and Rav Yeimar and Mar bar Rav Ashi gave opposite answers. The Sages reversed the attributions and sent the report to Rav Mordekhai. He sent word back to Mar bar Rav Ashi, recalling how Rav Ashi, standing with one foot on the step, had ruled a child's gift valid in every case.

15.actor: A man and his brother, in Mata Mehasya
15.event: A yevama fell to a man for levirate marriage and his brother wanted to disqualify her with a bill of divorce, so the man asked if it was about the property and offered to share it.
15.turn: The brother said he feared being cheated as in the Pumbedita swindler story.
15.outcome: The man offered to have the property divided right away, before he married the yevama.
15.summary: In Mata Mehasya, a man's brother wanted to disqualify the yevama who had fallen to the man by giving her a bill of divorce. The man asked whether this was over the property and offered to share it. The brother feared being cheated as in the earlier swindler story, so the man told him to divide the property right away if he wished.

16.actor: Rav Huna and his son Rabba
16.event: Rav Huna tore silk garments in front of his son Rabba to see whether he would get angry.
16.turn: The Gemara raises that this could cause his son to sin or destroy property.
16.summary: Rav Huna tore silk garments in front of his son Rabba, saying he wanted to see whether Rabba would become angry. The Gemara then explains why this was permitted.
16.missing: How the son reacted; the passage is an example used for a legal argument.

17.actor: Rav Pappa and Yehuda bar Mareimar
17.event: Rav Pappa went to write his son's marriage contract and pressed Yehuda bar Mareimar to enter the bride's father's house with him, though Yehuda did not want to because his presence would pressure the father to give a larger dowry.
17.turn: Yehuda entered and sat silent, so the father kept increasing the dowry until he had given everything he had.

18.missing: Reported rulings in cases and a scholarly exchange about them; no narrated event.

19.actor: Rav Shimi bar Hiyya and Rav
19.event: A man betrothed a woman with a bundle of rags and Rav Shimi examined it to see if it was worth a peruta.
19.turn: The Gemara objects that Shmuel would be concerned it might be worth a peruta elsewhere.
19.outcome: The objection is resolved by distinguishing certain from doubtful betrothal.
19.summary: A man betrothed a woman with a bundle of rags, and Rav Shimi bar Hiyya, sitting before Rav, checked whether it was worth a peruta. If it was, she was betrothed, and if not, she was not. The Gemara notes this appears to conflict with Shmuel and resolves it by distinguishing certain from uncertain betrothal.
19.missing: No actual outcome for the couple; it is a case used as legal precedent.

20.actor: Rav Yosef and two claimants to a field
20.event: Two deeds for the same field came before Rav Yosef, one dated the fifth of Nisan and one dated only 'Nisan', and he awarded the field to the holder of the dated deed.
20.turn: The holder of the undated deed protested, and Rav Yosef answered that his deed could be from the twenty-ninth of Nisan.
20.outcome: The man asked for a document to repossess other property, and Rav Yosef replied that a buyer could say his deed was from the first of Nisan.
20.summary: Two deeds for the same field came before Rav Yosef, one dated the fifth of Nisan and one just 'Nisan'. He awarded the field to the one with the specific date. The other man protested, and Rav Yosef said his deed could be from the twenty-ninth. When the man asked for a document to repossess property from later buyers, Rav Yosef said they could answer that his deed was from the first of Nisan.
